evidence_quotes.quote: The analysis shows that based on the area of Tanjungbalai city around 60.62 km2 with population 169.367 inhabitants and coverage services of PDAM Tirta Kualo in 2019 was only 68.86%.
The governance of sustainable drinking water supply in PDAM Tirta Kualo using governance principle based on the problems that exist in each working unit as presented in Table 2 and Table 3.

The sustainable water supply governance model designed to build improvement in the quality of infrastructures and human resources such as upgrading human resources, installing water meter to all customers, adding new water treatment plans in services area 5 and build free drinking water installation in open space area.
The respondence of the research are head of the family that already costumers for more than 10 years in all 5 coverage services areas of Tirta Kualo.
The total population in 2017 was 169.367 people, while the number of customers or house connections in 2017 was 23.320 customers.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal piped drinking water supply and household service coverage provided by PDAM Tirta Kualo across Tanjungbalai City.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain/literal broad wording of Criterion 2 because it examines internal utility administration and 'drinking water supply governance' across PDAM Tirta Kualo's five working units as well as alignment with the Tanjungbalai City spatial plan (2013-2033). However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2: 'governance' here consists of generic operational, technical, and human-resource issues (leaking pipes, damaged or missing water meters, lack of laboratory testing, low HR capacity, unpaid staff salaries), hydrological supply-demand calculations, and spatial land-use planning. Although Table 2 briefly notes in single diagnostic sentences that the utility is not at full cost recovery and has undetected illegal connections, the paper does not examine any tariff or cost-recovery rule, eligibility or tenure requirement, administrative burden, enforcement policy, or regulatory/ownership rule governing household service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Reports descriptive empirical data from PDAM Tirta Kualo administrative records (district-level customer connections and service coverage in Table 1; water meter conditions across 15,115 connections in Table 3) and qualitative interview findings from the utility's five working units (Table 2), alongside hydrological capacity and demand projections.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports district-level and citywide piped drinking water connection coverage (23,320 house connections serving 116,600 of 169,367 inhabitants, or 68.86% in Table 1; 71.37% cited in Section 1), water loss rate (36.86%), and projected water supply demand.
criterion_notes.c5: At the utility and district case-study level, the population/unit of analysis (PDAM Tirta Kualo and its 5 coverage areas / 6 districts in Tanjungbalai City), broad operational governance conditions, descriptive connection coverage outcomes, and mixed-methods descriptive case-study design are identifiable. Note that Section 2.1 mentions household heads who have been customers for over 10 years as respondents, but neither household sample sizes nor household survey results are reported, and no rule-type legal/governance exposure is linked to access outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English.

study_design: Mixed-methods descriptive case study (hydrological/demand projection, secondary utility administrative statistics, and interviews with utility working units)
population_and_sample: PDAM Tirta Kualo regional drinking water corporate and its 5 service coverage areas (6 districts; 169,367 inhabitants and 23,320 customer connections) in Tanjungbalai City, Indonesia; qualitative interviews with 5 utility working units (sample size not reported) and household customer respondents (>10 years tenure) mentioned in Methods (sample size and results not reported)
exposure: Internal utility operational/management conditions across 5 working units of PDAM Tirta Kualo (infrastructure maintenance, water meter condition, human resource capacity, SOP compliance) and municipal spatial planning (2013-2033); no rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism governing access is examined
outcome: Piped drinking water service coverage / house connections across 5 service areas (68.86% citywide in Table 1; 71.37% in text; 23,320 customer connections), water loss rate (36.86%), and projected water demand (liters/second)
rationale: Excluded under E03 (wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification. Although titled as a study of 'sustainable drinking water governance' and reporting municipal piped water coverage (68.86%), the empirical analysis consists of raw water capacity and population demand projections, a descriptive inventory of internal operational/technical/HR problems across PDAM Tirta Kualo's five working units (old pipes, broken/missing meters, low HR quality, lack of lab testing), and a normative upgrade model aligned with the municipal spatial plan. It does not examine any rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism (such as eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, administrative burdens, tariff/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, or regulatory/ownership structure) governing household service access. Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, it would be included as a descriptive mixed-methods case study of utility governance and service coverage.
